Case 3:25-cv-07947-CRB        Document 83       Filed 02/13/26    Page 1 of 2




                                   1
                                   2

                                   5                         IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
                                   6                     FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF CALIFORNIA
                                   7
                                   8    CHRISTOPHER MCPHEE, et al.,                    Case No. 25-cv-07947-CRB
                                   9                  Plaintiffs,
                                                                                       ORDER APPOINTING INTERIM
                                  10           v.                                      LEAD CLASS COUNSEL
                                  11    PROSPER FUNDING, LLC, et al.,
                                  12                  Defendants.
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13          On December 5, 2025, this Court consolidated twenty related cases and ordered
                                  14   applications for appointment of interim lead counsel to be filed within ten days.
                                  15   Order (dkt. 30) at 8. Twelve plaintiffs move for appointment of interim lead class counsel
                                  16   in this data breach case. Mots. (dkts. 39, 43, 44, 48, 49, 51, 52, 55–58, 63). The Court
                                  17   held a hearing on the matter on February 13, 2026. Minute Entry (dkt. 81). Based on the
                                  18   applicants’ oral and written arguments, and the factors of Rule 23(g)(1) of the Federal
                                  19   Rules of Civil Procedure, the Court APPOINTS Gibbs Mura LLP (“Gibbs”) and Hausfeld
                                  20   LLP (“Hausfeld”) as interim co-lead counsel.
                                  21          Rule 23(g)(3) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure authorizes the Court to
                                  22   “designate interim counsel to act on behalf of a putative class before determining whether
                                  23   to certify the actions as a class action.” The Court must consider four factors in appointing
                                  24   interim counsel: (1) “the work counsel has done in identifying or investigating potential
                                  25   claims in the action”; (2) “counsel’s experience in handling class actions, other complex
                                  26   litigation, and the types of claims asserted in the action”; (3) “counsel’s knowledge of the
                                  27   applicable law”; and (4) “the resources that counsel will commit to representing the class.”
                                  28   Fed. R. Civ. P. 23(g)(1)(A); see also In re Lenovo Adware Litig., No. 15-md-2624, 2015
                                         Case 3:25-cv-07947-CRB          Document 83       Filed 02/13/26    Page 2 of 2




                                   1   WL 10890657, at *1 n.1 (N.D. Cal. July 27, 2015) (applying the Rule 23(g)(1)(A) factors
                                   2   to appointments of interim counsel). The Court may also “consider any other matter
                                   3   pertinent to counsel’s ability to fairly and adequately represent the interests of the class.”
                                   4   Fed. R. Civ. P. 23(g)(1)(B); see also In re Lenovo Adware Litig., 2015 WL 10890657, at
                                   5   *1–2 (considering candidates’ location, ability to work cooperatively with others, and
                                   6   ability to maintain reasonable fees and expenses).
                                   7          These factors all support appointment of Gibbs and Hausfeld. First, Gibbs and
                                   8   Hausfeld have investigated the facts, interviewed class representatives, explored retaining
                                   9   experts in the relevant fields, and identified potential causes of action. Gibbs-Hausfeld
                                  10   Mot. (dkt. 58) at 3. Second, each firm has extensive experience leading data breach class
                                  11   actions. See id. at 4–7; id. Exs. A–B. Third, each firm seeks to appoint an attorney with
                                  12   specialized experience in data breach class actions, demonstrating each firm’s knowledge
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   of the law. Id. at 4–7. Fourth, both firms have significant resources available to commit to
                                  14   this case, and each has a large, specialized data breach practice group. Id. at 8.
                                  15          Other considerations also weigh in favor of appointing Gibbs and Hausfeld. Gibbs
                                  16   is a local firm and proposes a local attorney. Id. at 10. Additionally, appointment of two
                                  17   firms is appropriate as, at the February 13 hearing, counsel seeking appointment estimated
                                  18   that the class size could be as large as 17.6 million individuals. See id. at 9.
                                  19          For the foregoing reasons, the Court appoints Gibbs and Hausfeld as interim co-lead
                                  20   counsel. The Court further appoints David Berger and James Pizzirusso as the designated
                                  21   lead attorneys from each firm.
                                  22          IT IS SO ORDERED.
                                  23          Dated: February 13, 2026
                                                                                          CHARLES R. BREYER
                                  24                                                      United States District Judge
